title: Prepending a tagged arrow acts on reduced categorical words
statement:
Let $O$ be a small set and $A,B$ small categories [def-nagata-category] with object set $O$. A tagged arrow is an arrow in either $A$ or $B$, with its factor recorded. For $x,z\in O$, let $R(x,z)$ be the set of finite composable lists from $x$ to $z$ of tagged nonidentity arrows whose consecutive tags differ; the empty list $\varepsilon_x$ belongs to $R(x,x)$. For a tagged arrow $f:x\to y$ in factor $t\in\{A,B\}$, including an identity arrow, and $w\in R(y,z)$, define $P_f(w)$ by the following rules. If $f=\mathrm{id}_x$, put $P_f(w)=w$. Otherwise, if $w$ is empty or its first tag differs from $t$, prepend $f$ to $w$. Otherwise write $w=g\,w'$ with $g:y\to u$ in factor $t$, form $c=g\circ f$ in that factor, and put $P_f(w)=w'$ if $c=\mathrm{id}_x$ and $P_f(w)=c\,w'$ otherwise. Identity cases identify the equal endpoint objects. These rules define a map $P_f:R(y,z)\to R(x,z)$ for every $z\in O$. For every tagged identity and every pair $f:x\to y$, $g:y\to u$ in the same factor, they satisfy
$$P_{\mathrm{id}_x}(w)=w,\qquad P_f(P_g(w))=P_{g\circ f}(w)\quad(w\in R(u,z)).$$
No freeness hypothesis and no restriction on invertible arrows or on composites equal to identities is imposed.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof of Proposition 3.2, printed p.21, unique alternating factorization; agent expansion of the prepend-action law from the returned normal-form proof, step 2. No Stacks tag states this typed categorical action law.

proof.text: First check that the rules produce reduced composable words. An identity input preserves the word and identifies $x=y$. If the input $f$ is nonidentity and the word is empty or begins in the other factor, adjoining $f$ gives the required alternating nonidentity list with source $x$. In the remaining case write $w=h\,v$, where $h:y\to a$ has the tag of $f$ and $v$ is empty or begins in the other factor. The composite $h\circ f:x\to a$ is defined by [def-nagata-category]. If it is nonidentity, its tag differs from the first tag of $v$, so $(h\circ f)\,v$ is reduced. If it is an identity, $a=x$, and $v$ is already a reduced word from $x$ to $z$. These mutually exclusive cases give a single value in $R(x,z)$; no iteration or choice of reductions is used.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof of Proposition 3.2, printed p.21; agent expansion of the categorical prepend-action law, case 1.

proof.text: The identity rule gives $P_{\mathrm{id}_x}(w)=w$ directly. To prove the composition law, fix $f:x\to y$ and $g:y\to u$ in one factor $t$. If $f$ is an identity, $P_f(P_g(w))=P_g(w)=P_{g\circ f}(w)$ by the right identity law in [def-nagata-category]. If $g$ is an identity, $P_f(P_g(w))=P_f(w)=P_{g\circ f}(w)$ by the left identity law. Hence assume both $f$ and $g$ nonidentity and put $c=g\circ f$.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof of Proposition 3.2, printed p.21; agent expansion of the categorical prepend-action law, case 2.

proof.text: Suppose $w$ is empty or its first tag differs from $t$. Then $P_g(w)=g\,w$. Applying $P_f$ merges $f$ with this first letter: it gives $w$ if $c$ is an identity and $c\,w$ otherwise. These are exactly the two values of $P_c(w)$ under the rules in the statement (in the identity case $x=u$). Thus the composition law holds in this case.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof of Proposition 3.2, printed p.21; agent expansion of the categorical prepend-action law, case 3.

proof.text: Otherwise write $w=h\,v$ with $h:u\to a$ a nonidentity arrow in factor $t$; the reduced tail $v$ is empty or begins with the other tag. Put $d=h\circ g:y\to a$. First suppose $d$ nonidentity. Then $P_g(w)=d\,v$, and $P_f(P_g(w))$ is $v$ if $e=d\circ f$ is an identity and $e\,v$ otherwise. Associativity in [def-nagata-category] gives $e=(h\circ g)\circ f=h\circ(g\circ f)=h\circ c$. If $c$ is nonidentity, the rule for $P_c(h\,v)$ gives exactly those same two outputs. If $c=\mathrm{id}_x$, then $x=u$, $e=h\circ\mathrm{id}_x=h$ is nonidentity, and both sides equal $h\,v=w$.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof of Proposition 3.2, printed p.21; agent expansion of the categorical prepend-action law, case 4.

proof.text: Finally suppose $d=h\circ g=\mathrm{id}_y$, so $a=y$ and $P_g(w)=v$. Since $f$ is nonidentity and $v$ is empty or begins with the other tag, $P_f(P_g(w))=f\,v$. If $c=g\circ f$ is nonidentity, associativity and the identity law in [def-nagata-category] give $h\circ c=(h\circ g)\circ f=f$, which is nonidentity, so $P_c(h\,v)=f\,v$. If $c=\mathrm{id}_x$, then $x=u$ and $f=(h\circ g)\circ f=h\circ(g\circ f)=h$, again by those axioms. Consequently $P_c(w)=w=h\,v=f\,v$. Together with the previous cases this proves the law for every $w$. The argument includes noninvertible retractions as well as inverse pairs; it never infers $g\circ h=\mathrm{id}$ from $h\circ g=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof of Proposition 3.2, printed p.21; agent expansion of the categorical prepend-action law, case 5.

lean.statement: theorem reduced_word_prepend_action {O : Type u} (A B : Category.{v} O) : (∀ (x z : O) (w : ReducedWord A B (x := x) (z := z)), prependLeft (identity A x) w = w) ∧ (∀ (x z : O) (w : ReducedWord A B (x := x) (z := z)), prependRight (identity B x) w = w) ∧ (∀ (x y u z : O) (f : Hom A x y) (g : Hom A y u) (w : ReducedWord A B (x := u) (z := z)), prependLeft f (prependLeft g w) = prependLeft (compose A f g) w) ∧ (∀ (x y u z : O) (f : Hom B x y) (g : Hom B y u) (w : ReducedWord A B (x := u) (z := z)), prependRight f (prependRight g w) = prependRight (compose B f g) w)
